The seat ran in a Claude Code cloud container from 2026-10-18 22:38 UTC: Opus 5.5, Linux x64, Node v24.12.0. The
machine check printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib`, which matches the brief, and
`tools/test_budget.py` printed 1 (and `--mutants` 1), so every vitest run used `--maxWorkers=1` and the mutants ran one
at a time. The seat is an implementer-side closing checker. It wrote no part of the item: it is not the author (L-0048),
a fixer (L-0051, L-0447, L-0552 for this round's `build/M0-m-01-fix-s1`) or an earlier checker (L-0050, L-0054,
L-0454). Its ledger row is L-0553 in `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2.

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item. It wrote this file, rows N-s1-1 – N-s1-3 of `checks/M0-m-01-notes.md`, its CLEAN-ROOM
  row, its two landed records and its lane-log lines. It ran no git command. The verdict file is `checks/M0-m-01-s1.md`
  (J269); `checks/M0-m-01.md` and `checks/M0-m-01-c1.md` stay as committed.
* **The before tree, without git.** A Python reader of its own read the model package's files from `.git/index` and
  the object packs (plain file reads; HEAD ab2e334). Of the item's owned files, 8 differ from those blobs: exactly the 8

  `stage/index.ts`, `test/types/types.test.ts`, `test/types/narration.ts` (new), `test/records/records.test.ts`,
  `test/stage/stage.test.ts`). The mirror was a copy of `plat/` under the lane's scratch folder
  (`waves/check-M0-m-01/mirror`), installed `--frozen-lockfile --offline`, isolated (0 links out of the copy), each
  mutant restored and `cmp`-checked before the next. It is deleted at the end, node_modules first.
* **The relaunch.** The seat's session was relaunched mid-lane (2026-10-19 01:30); the container was the same, so the
  mirror, the mutant log, the census output and the RELATED log written by this lane were present and read back (the
  CONTINUE RULE). The gates were re-run in the tree after the relaunch (section (2)).
* **Disclosure.** The resume rule's grep of the lane log printed the builder's CHECKPOINT and LANDED lines. The notes

  before the seat's mutants were planned; it carries the author's mutant names. The seat's 38 mutants are its own list

## (1) The failing lines of the round, one by one

### N-c1-1 (`checks/M0-m-01-notes.md:83`, inventory `M0-m-01:83`) — no-narration guard over src only by a deny-list: FIXED, PINNED; the shared home REPORTED

Source note, read whole: the guard scanned `model/src/{types,records,schema,stage}` only; the item's own tests were
outside it ("(the check's N-2)" in `types.test.ts` would not have been caught) and narration phrased otherwise escaped
("added in wave 3 by the author"). Fix shape: extend the scan to `test/{types,records,schema,stage}` and share one
pattern list with the other packages' guards.

* **The code.** `test/types/narration.ts` exports one list (`NARRATION`, eleven named patterns, each with a probe;
  `narrationIn(line)`; `NARRATION_CAUGHT` lines that must match; `DESIGN_WORDS` lines that must pass). The guard in
  `types.test.ts` (title kept: "no comment narrates a round, a check or a landing …") scans `src/` and `test/` of the
  four folders and asserts the scan reached named files of both trees.
* **Pins, the checker's mutants (mirror):**

  | mutant | what | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | X1 | "(the checker's probe)" in `test/schema/schema.test.ts`'s header comment | RED: `test/schema/schema.test.ts:1: … expected [ 'a check or its checker' ] to deeply equal []` |
  | X2 | "added in wave 3 by the author" in `src/records/walls.ts`'s comment (the note's own probe) | RED: `src/records/walls.ts:1: … expected [ …(3) ] to deeply equal []` |
  | X3 | a lane key in `test/stage/stage.test.ts`'s header | RED: `expected [ 'a lane key' ] …` |
  | X4 | "(kept since round 3)" in the QuarterNode `it` title | RED: `expected [ 'a round, a pass or a phase' ] …` |
  | X5 | "formerly spelt in each" in `src/stage/lifecycle.ts`'s comment | RED: `expected [ 'what a line used to be' ] …` |
  | X6 | the guard's scan drops the test folders (the C1 scope) | RED: `expected [ 'src/types/identity.ts', …(18) ] to include 'test/types/types.test.ts'` |
  | X7 | the lane-key pattern removed from the list | RED: `see check/M0-m-01-close-s1: expected [] to not deeply equal []` |
  | X8 | the landing pattern widened to `\blanding\b` | RED: `test/types/narration.ts:15: … expected [ 'a landing' ] …` (DESIGN_WORDS holds the sky landing) |
  | X10 | narration in `narration.ts`'s own comment | RED: `test/types/narration.ts:7: … expected [ 'a change told as history' ] …` |
  | X9 | the list file's comments-only exemption widened to every file, with X4's line planted | SURVIVED (vitest exit 0) — judged below |

* **Without the fix.** The round-C1 guard (the before blobs) with X1 + X2 planted: 35 of 35 green, exit 0 — the escapes
  the note names; on the round's sources the same lines are red (X1, X2). The round's new tests on the before sources:
  `tsc` 6 errors (2 × TS2305, 3 × TS2694, 1 × TS2589) and vitest 5 failed of 43.
* **"Share one pattern list".** The list is one exported module. A search inside `plat/` (`grep -rlin narrat packages

  `types.test.ts`: no other package has a guard to share it with yet, and a test project may not import model's

  REPORTED for the session's ruling with that reason (notes 'Hardening round S1', C-0371 (1)); by the round's rule (1)
  a half that needs another item's file is reported, not built, and it is not a failing line.
* **X9, judged.** X9 is a mutant of the pin itself (the guard's own code), not of the item's code: it narrows the guard

### N-c1-2 (`checks/M0-m-01-notes.md:84`, inventory `M0-m-01:84`) — import-path guard reads declarations only: FIXED, PINNED

Source note, read whole: the guard read the module specifiers of `import` / `export` declarations only; an inline type
query `import('../types/identity.js').Lifecycle` in a type position would carry a second path past it. Fix shape: walk
`ImportTypeNode`s too (`ts.isImportTypeNode`, its `argument.literal.text`) under the same rule.

* **The code.** `moduleSpecifiers(sf)` in `types.test.ts` walks the whole tree: declarations, `import x = require`,
  `ImportTypeNode` (its `argument.literal`), a dynamic `import()`; a non-literal specifier is reported `<computed>` and
  fails the rule; the message names file and line.
* **Pins, the checker's mutants:**

  | mutant | what | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | I1 | `lifecycle: import('../types/identity.js').Lifecycle` in `records/site.ts` (the note's probe) | RED: `records/site.ts:76 imports '../types/identity.js': expected false to be true` |
  | I2 | `typeof import('../stage/vocab.js')` nested in a generic in `schema/order.ts` | RED: `schema/order.ts:10 imports '../stage/vocab.js'` |
  | I3 | an inline type import of `'../types/kernel.js'` in a field type of `stage/decl.ts` | RED: `stage/decl.ts:87 imports '../types/kernel.js'` |
  | I4 | a dynamic `import('../schema/order.js')` in `stage/lifecycle.ts` | RED: `stage/lifecycle.ts:11 imports '../schema/order.js'` |
  | I5 | the `ImportTypeNode` branch removed from the walk | RED: `expected [ { …(2) }, …(4) ] to deeply equal [ { …(2) }, …(6) ]` |
  | I6 | the walk over top-level statements only | RED: `expected [ { …(2) }, …(2) ] to deeply equal [ … …(6) ]` |

* **Without the fix.** The round-C1 guard with I1 planted: green (in the 35 of 35 run above, exit 0).

Outcome: **FIXED**, **PINNED** (I1 – I6 red).

## Refusal census (J264, N-58), re-measured

The checker's own runtime probe (`census.mjs`, imported once against the before sources and once against the tree's)
over the item's operations — `schemaOrder` over the 15 M0 kinds and 5 kinds with no M0 schema; `lawLimit` over 6 laws
× 21 counts and 7 bad inputs; after, also `generatedLifecycle` over 10 whole epochs (0, −0, …, 2^53 − 1) and 8 bad ones:

| | lawful | lawful refused | unlawful | unlawful refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 120 | 0 | 12 + 21 | 12 |
| after | 130 | 0 | 20 + 21 | 20 |

The probe's sixth law (`perUnit −2`) is not lawful — the table door refuses such a row (`tables/src/workLimits/table.ts:71`,
"perUnit must be a number ≥ 0") — so its 21 rows are counted unlawful (the "+ 21"); `lawLimit` itself returns a
negative limit for them before and after (the round did not touch `vocab.ts`): notes N-s1-3, M4. **Lawful refusals 0 → 0:
the census did not rise.** Every refusal seen is UNLAWFUL → REFUSE, a typed RangeError naming the value (e.g.
`generatedLifecycle: epoch 0.5 is not a whole number ≥ 0`, `lawLimit: count NaN for 'a'`); the kinds, laws and epochs
are the build's own values, so no user reaches them through §11.4's doors. No lawful-input refusal was seen, so none
is routed to the session.
